Check it: reload the admin. Posts appears in the sidebar, and in the ⌘K / Ctrl+K command palette. Clicking it shows a 404 page saying the controller is not found. You'll write it next.

docs.title: Step 4: Show a page
docs.text:
Admin controllers extend Bonfire\Core\AdminController, which renders views inside the Admin theme. Create app/Modules/Blog/Controllers/PostController.php:

<?php

namespace App\Modules\Blog\Controllers;

use Bonfire\Core\AdminController;

class PostController extends AdminController
{
    public function list()
    {
        return $this->render('App\Modules\Blog\Views\list');
    }
}

Create the view at app/Modules/Blog/Views/list.php. It extends the theme's master layout and fills its main section, using two view components: <x-page-head> for the page title and <x-admin-box> for a card to hold the content.

<?php $this->extend('master') ?>

<?php $this->section('main') ?>
<x-page-head title="Posts" />

<x-admin-box>
    <p>Your posts will be listed here.</p>
</x-admin-box>
<?php $this->endSection() ?>

Check it: click Posts in the sidebar. You get a page titled "Posts" inside the admin layout, and the menu item is marked as the current page.

docs.title: Step 5: Protect it with a permission
docs.text:
Right now anyone who can reach the admin can open this page. Bonfire uses Shield permissions to control access. You'll require a posts.list permission for the page.

First, require it. Add a permission to the menu item in Module.php, so users without it don't see the link:

$item = new MenuItem([
    'title'           => 'Posts',
    'namedRoute'      => 'posts-list',
    'fontAwesomeIcon' => 'fas fa-newspaper',
    'permission'      => 'posts.list',
]);

Hiding the link doesn't stop anyone typing the URL, so check the permission in the controller too:

public function list()
{
    if (! auth()->user()->can('posts.list')) {
        return redirect()->to(ADMIN_AREA)->with('error', lang('Bonfire.notAuthorized'));
    }

    return $this->render('App\Modules\Blog\Views\list');
}

Reload the admin. Posts has disappeared from the sidebar, and /admin/posts sends you back to the dashboard: the permission doesn't exist yet, so no one has it, not even a superadmin.

Now declare the permission, and grant it to groups, from the module itself. Create app/Modules/Blog/Config/Registrar.php:

<?php

namespace App\Modules\Blog\Config;

class Registrar
{
    public static function AuthGroups(): array
    {
        return [
            'permissions' => [
                'posts.list' => 'Can view the list of blog posts',
            ],
            'moduleGrants' => [
                'blog' => [
                    'superadmin' => ['posts.*'],
                    'admin'      => ['posts.list'],
                ],
            ],
        ];
    }
}

CodeIgniter only reads a Config/Registrar.php at the root of a namespace it knows about. Tell it about the module's namespace in app/Config/Autoload.php:

public $psr4 = [
    APP_NAMESPACE      => APPPATH,
    'App\Modules\Blog' => APPPATH . 'Modules/Blog',
];

The permission now exists. Apply the default grants to the groups:

php spark bonfire:permissions

It reports Added 2 permission grant(s).

Check it: reload the admin. Posts is back in the sidebar, and the page opens again. In Settings › User Groups, open the Superadmin group's permissions: posts.list is ticked.

Permissions explains the registrar and the grants command in more depth.

docs.title: Step 6: List the posts
docs.text:
Now put real data on the page. Create a model at app/Modules/Blog/Models/PostModel.php. Soft deletes mean a deleted post keeps its row with a deleted_at date, and the model leaves it out of results:

<?php

namespace App\Modules\Blog\Models;

use CodeIgniter\Model;

class PostModel extends Model
{
    protected $table          = 'posts';
    protected $returnType     = 'object';
    protected $useSoftDeletes = true;
    protected $useTimestamps  = true;
    protected $allowedFields  = ['title', 'status'];
}

Update the controller to load a page of posts. setting('Site.perPage') is the page size, from app/Config/Site.php:

<?php

namespace App\Modules\Blog\Controllers;

use App\Modules\Blog\Models\PostModel;
use Bonfire\Core\AdminController;

class PostController extends AdminController
{
    public function list()
    {
        if (! auth()->user()->can('posts.list')) {
            return redirect()->to(ADMIN_AREA)->with('error', lang('Bonfire.notAuthorized'));
        }

        $model = model(PostModel::class);

        return $this->render('App\Modules\Blog\Views\list', [
            'posts' => $model->orderBy('created_at', 'desc')->paginate(setting('Site.perPage')),
            'pager' => $model->pager,
            'total' => $model->pager->getTotal(),
        ]);
    }
}

Put the table in its own view, app/Modules/Blog/Views/_table.php. In step 7 the search and filters will reload just this part of the page. It uses three more components and helpers:

  • <x-status> shows each post's status as a coloured dot and label.
  • <x-empty-state> takes the table's place when nothing matches.
  • The bonfire_list_hx pager template adds the "Showing X of Y · Previous / Next" footer.
<?php if ($posts === []) : ?>
    <x-empty-state title="No posts match" hint="Try a different search or filter." />
<?php else : ?>
    <div class="table-responsive">
        <table class="table table-hover bf-table">
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Title</th>
                    <th>Status</th>
                    <th>Created</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
            <?php foreach ($posts as $post) : ?>
                <tr>
                    <td><?= esc($post->title) ?></td>
                    <td>
                        <x-status tone="<?= $post->status === 'published' ? 'ok' : 'muted' ?>" label="<?= esc(ucfirst($post->status)) ?>" />
                    </td>
                    <td><?= app_date($post->created_at) ?></td>
                </tr>
            <?php endforeach ?>
            </tbody>
        </table>
    </div>

    <?= $pager->links('default', 'bonfire_list_hx') ?>
<?php endif ?>

Then include it from list.php, and show the total beside the title with the page head's count:

<?php $this->extend('master') ?>

<?php $this->section('main') ?>
<x-page-head title="Posts" count="<?= $total ?>" />

<x-admin-box>
    <div id="content-list" hx-target="#content-list">
        <?= $this->include('App\Modules\Blog\Views\_table') ?>
    </div>
</x-admin-box>
<?php $this->endSection() ?>

The pager's Previous / Next links load the next page with htmx and swap it into the element named by the nearest hx-target, here #content-list.

Check it: the page lists six posts with green "Published" and grey "Draft" labels, and a count of 6 beside the title. "A post nobody needs" is missing because it is deleted. The footer reads "Showing 6 of 6".

docs.title: Step 7: Add search and filters
docs.text:
Bonfire draws a filter panel from a list of filters declared on a model. Add them to a model of their own, so PostModel stays plain. Create app/Modules/Blog/Models/PostFilter.php:

<?php

namespace App\Modules\Blog\Models;

use Bonfire\Core\Traits\Filterable;

class PostFilter extends PostModel
{
    use Filterable;

    protected $filters = [
        'status' => [
            'title'   => 'Status',
            'options' => ['draft' => 'Draft', 'published' => 'Published'],
        ],
    ];
}

Each key of $filters is a column. Its options become checkboxes, and the Filterable trait's filter() method turns the checked ones into a WHERE status IN (…). Filters covers radio buttons and options computed by a method.

Update the controller. It applies the filters and the search term from the query string. When htmx asks for the list (the request has an HX-Request header), it returns only _table, which htmx swaps into the page:

<?php

namespace App\Modules\Blog\Controllers;

use App\Modules\Blog\Models\PostFilter;
use Bonfire\Core\AdminController;

class PostController extends AdminController
{
    public function list()
    {
        if (! auth()->user()->can('posts.list')) {
            return redirect()->to(ADMIN_AREA)->with('error', lang('Bonfire.notAuthorized'));
        }

        $model  = model(PostFilter::class);
        $search = trim((string) $this->request->getGet('search'));

        $model->filter($this->request->getGet('filters'));

        if ($search !== '') {
            $model->like('title', $search);
        }

        $isHtmx = $this->request->hasHeader('HX-Request');

        return $this->render('App\Modules\Blog\Views\\' . ($isHtmx ? '_table' : 'list'), [
            'posts'  => $model->orderBy('created_at', 'desc')->paginate(setting('Site.perPage')),
            'pager'  => $model->pager,
            'total'  => $model->pager->getTotal(),
            'search' => $search,
        ]);
    }
}

Finally, add the toolbar and filter panel to list.php:

<?php $this->extend('master') ?>

<?php $this->section('main') ?>
<x-page-head title="Posts" count="<?= $total ?>" />

<x-admin-box>
    <div x-data="{filtered: false}" hx-target="#content-list" hx-include=".bf-toolbar-form, .filters .filter-check">
        <div class="bf-toolbar">
            <form class="bf-toolbar-form" action="<?= current_url() ?>" method="get"
                hx-get="<?= current_url() ?>"
                hx-trigger="input delay:300ms from:[name=search]">
                <div class="bf-toolbar-search">
                    <i class="fas fa-search" aria-hidden="true"></i>
                    <input type="search" name="search" class="form-control" value="<?= esc($search) ?>"
                        placeholder="Search posts" aria-label="Search posts">
                </div>
            </form>
            <x-filter-link />
        </div>

        <div class="bf-list-with-filters">
            <div id="content-list">
                <?= $this->include('App\Modules\Blog\Views\_table') ?>
            </div>

            <div class="bf-filter-panel" x-cloak x-show="filtered" x-transition.duration.240ms>
                <?= view_cell('Bonfire\Core\Cells\Filters::renderList', 'model=App\Modules\Blog\Models\PostFilter target=#content-list') ?>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>
</x-admin-box>
<?php $this->endSection() ?>

Here is what each part does:

  • x-data="{filtered: false}" is Alpine.js state for whether the filter panel is open. <x-filter-link> toggles it, and x-show="filtered" shows or hides the panel.
  • The search form sends a request 300 ms after you stop typing, with hx-get and hx-trigger.
  • The Filters::renderList view cell draws the checkboxes from PostFilter::$filters, and sends a request whenever one changes.
  • hx-include on the wrapper sends the search box and the checked filters with every request, so the search, the filters and the pager all keep each other's values.
  • hx-target puts each response into #content-list.

Check it: type team in the search box. Without a page reload, the list narrows to "Meet the team" and the footer reads "Showing 1 of 1". Clear the search, open the filters, and tick Draft: two drafts remain. Tick Published and search for the: only "Meet the team" is left.

docs.title: Step 8: Appear in the global search
docs.text:
The search box in the admin header searches every module that provides a SearchProvider class at its root. Create app/Modules/Blog/SearchProvider.php:

<?php

namespace App\Modules\Blog;

use App\Modules\Blog\Models\PostModel;
use Bonfire\Search\Interfaces\SearchProviderInterface;

class SearchProvider extends PostModel implements SearchProviderInterface
{
    public function search(string $term, int $limit = 10, ?array $post = null): array
    {
        if (! auth()->user()->can('posts.list')) {
            return [];
        }

        return $this->like('title', $term)
            ->orderBy('created_at', 'desc')
            ->findAll($limit);
    }

    public function resourceName(): string
    {
        return 'posts';
    }

    public function resourceUrl(): string
    {
        return ADMIN_AREA . '/posts';
    }

    public function resultView(): string
    {
        return 'Search/posts';
    }
}

search() returns the matching posts. Bonfire asks every provider, whoever is searching, so the provider checks the permission itself. resourceName() heads this module's results, resourceUrl() is the "See all" link, and resultView() names the view that shows the results.

That view must be in the Admin theme. Create themes/Admin/Search/posts.php. The results arrive as $rows:

<div class="table-responsive">
    <table class="table table-hover bf-table">
        <tbody>
        <?php foreach ($rows as $post) : ?>
            <tr>
                <td><?= esc($post->title) ?></td>
                <td><x-status tone="<?= $post->status === 'published' ? 'ok' : 'muted' ?>" label="<?= esc(ucfirst($post->status)) ?>" /></td>
            </tr>
        <?php endforeach ?>
        </tbody>
    </table>
</div>

Check it: type tips in the search box in the admin header and press Enter. The results page has a Posts section listing "Ten tips for faster pages", with a "See all posts" link back to your list.

Search shows how to search related tables and meta fields.

docs.title: Step 9: Send deleted posts to the Recycler
docs.text:
The Recycler under Tools lists soft-deleted records so an admin can restore or purge them. It only shows the models it has been told about. Register PostModel in initAdmin(), with the columns that help someone recognise a post:

<?php

namespace App\Modules\Blog;

use App\Modules\Blog\Models\PostModel;
use Bonfire\Core\BaseModule;
use Bonfire\Menus\MenuItem;

class Module extends BaseModule
{
    public function initAdmin()
    {
        $item = new MenuItem([
            'title'           => 'Posts',
            'namedRoute'      => 'posts-list',
            'fontAwesomeIcon' => 'fas fa-newspaper',
            'permission'      => 'posts.list',
        ]);
        service('menus')->menu('sidebar')->collection('content')->addItem($item);

        service('recycler')->register('posts', 'Posts', PostModel::class, ['title', 'status']);
    }
}

To restore a post, the Recycler sets its deleted_at back to null through the model, and a model only writes the fields listed in $allowedFields. Add deleted_at to them in PostModel:

protected $allowedFields  = ['title', 'status', 'deleted_at'];

Check it: open Tools › Recycler and pick Posts from the list of resources. "A post nobody needs" is there. Click Restore, then go back to Posts: the list now shows seven posts.

docs.title: What you built
docs.text:
Your Blog module is a complete, if small, admin screen:

  • Module.php adds the sidebar item and registers posts with the Recycler.
  • Config/Routes.php maps /admin/posts to the controller.
  • Config/Registrar.php declares the posts.list permission and grants it to superadmins and admins.
  • PostController checks the permission and renders the full page, or only the table for htmx.
  • PostModel soft-deletes posts, and PostFilter adds the status filter.
  • list.php and _table.php build the page from the admin theme's components.
  • SearchProvider and themes/Admin/Search/posts.php add posts to the global search.

docs.title: View Components
docs.text:
View Components (or just Components) allow you to create custom HTML elements to use within your views. The main description of their use and creating new ones is described within the Building Sites section of the guide. This page lists the components that are available within the default Admin theme.

Your app renders its own copy of these components, in themes/Admin/Components/, which composer update doesn't change. See Why Themes Are Published Into Your App.

Escape attribute values with esc() (title="<?= esc($user->name()) ?>"), as you would any HTML attribute. The renderer decodes them and the component escapes them again on output, so a quote in the data can't end the attribute early. On a paired tag (<x-…>…</x-…>) a value can't contain >. Slots are HTML and are output as given.

docs.title: Page structure
docs.text:
<x-page-head>

The page header. Give it a title and it renders the design's head: an <h1>, an optional count badge or subtitle, an optional back link (backLabel names it, defaulting to "Back"), and the slot as actions on the right.

<x-page-head title="Users" count="<?= $total ?>">
    <a href="<?= url_to('user-new') ?>" class="btn btn-primary">New user</a>
</x-page-head>

<x-page-head title="<?= esc($user->displayName()) ?>" back="<?= esc(site_url(ADMIN_AREA . '/users')) ?>" backLabel="<?= esc(lang('Users.usersModTitle')) ?>" />

Without a title it wraps the slot as before, so existing <x-page-head><h2>…</h2></x-page-head> headers keep working.

<x-admin-box>

A card section. The optional title and description render a header. Setting rows and tables inside it run edge to edge; put buttons in a <div class="bf-card-footer"> as the last child for a footer.

<x-admin-box title="Site" description="How the site presents itself.">
    …
</x-admin-box>

<x-tabs>

Underline tabs. The slot holds Bootstrap nav-item list items, so service('resourceTabs')->renderTabsFor() output fits in it.

<x-tabs>
    <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link active" href="<?= $user->adminLink() ?>">Details</a></li>
    <?= service('resourceTabs')->renderTabsFor('user') ?>
</x-tabs>

<x-settings-layout>

The frame of a settings page: a "Settings" page head, a sub-nav of the sidebar's settings collection (only the pages the user may open, the current one marked), and the slot beside it. Register your module's settings page in that collection and wrap the page in it.

<x-settings-layout>
    <form action="<?= site_url(ADMIN_AREA . '/settings/blog') ?>" method="post">
        <?= csrf_field() ?>
        <x-admin-box title="Posts">…</x-admin-box>
        <x-save-bar />
    </form>
</x-settings-layout>

<x-sidebar>

The admin sidebar: the site's brand, a Dashboard link, then the sidebar menu's collections and items that the current user may see, with the current page marked. It takes no attributes. The Admin layout (master.php) renders it once, so you don't place it yourself: add your module's links to the sidebar menu instead (see Menus).

<x-sidebar />

docs.title: Settings forms
docs.text:
<x-setting-row>

A label and description on the left, the control (the slot) on the right. Wraps on narrow screens. for points the label at the control's id.

<x-setting-row label="Site name" description="Shown in the admin." for="siteName">
    <input type="text" class="form-control" id="siteName" name="siteName" value="<?= esc($siteName) ?>">
</x-setting-row>

<x-switch>

An accessible role="switch" checkbox. A hidden input posts offValue (default 0) when it is off; value (default 1) posts when it is on. Give it an empty offValue to post nothing when off, as for an array name like permissions[] that should hold only the checked values. checked turns it on unless it is empty, 0 or false; label becomes its aria-label. Any other attribute (id, x-model, disabled, …) goes on the checkbox.

<x-switch name="siteOnline" label="Site online" checked="<?= setting('Site.siteOnline') ? '1' : '' ?>" />
<x-switch name="permissions[]" offValue value="users.edit" checked="<?= $canEdit ? '1' : '' ?>" />

<x-segmented>

A radio group styled as a segmented control. options is a JSON object of value => label; wrap it in single quotes.

<x-segmented name="timeFormat" label="Time format" value="<?= $timeFormat ?>"
    options='<?= json_encode(['g:i A' => '12-hour', 'H:i' => '24-hour'], JSON_HEX_APOS) ?>' />

<x-save-bar>

A sticky "Unsaved changes · Discard · Save" bar for long forms. Put it inside the <form>: it appears once a field changes, Discard resets the form, and Save submits it. save relabels the Save button. Without JavaScript it is always shown, so the form can still be submitted.

<form method="post" action="…">
    …
    <x-save-bar save="Save settings" />
</form>

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
<x-chip>

A pill filter with an optional count. With an href it is a link (active marks the current one). With a name it is a radio input for a filter form, checked when active; give the chips one name and each its own value. With neither it is a toggle button. Other attributes (hx-get, hx-target, …) pass through.

<x-chip label="Admins" count="3" href="?group=admin" active="<?= $group === 'admin' ? '1' : '' ?>" />

<x-chip name="role" value="admin" label="Admins" count="3" active="<?= $role === 'admin' ? '1' : '' ?>" />

<x-status>

A coloured dot and a label. tone is ok, warn, danger, info or muted (the default).

<x-status tone="ok" label="Active" />

<x-empty-state>

A centered title and optional hint for a list with nothing in it.

<x-empty-state title="No users match" hint="Try a different search or group." />

<x-selection-bar>

A sticky bar showing "N selected" while any row checkbox (tbody input[type=checkbox]) in its form is checked. The slot holds the bulk actions; the ✕ clears the selection.

<form method="post">
    <?= csrf_field() ?>
    <table class="table">…</table>
    <x-selection-bar>
        <x-bulk-actions list="users" />
    </x-selection-bar>
</form>

<x-bulk-actions>

The bulk actions of the list, as buttons that post the form's checked selects[]. Place it inside <x-selection-bar>.

<x-row-actions>

A row's menu: its slot (links like Edit), then the row actions of the list for the record id.

<x-row-actions list="users" id="<?= $user->id ?>">
    <li><a href="<?= $user->adminLink() ?>" class="dropdown-item">Edit</a></li>
</x-row-actions>

<x-confirm-dialog> and <x-action-run>

Both sit once in the Admin layout (master.php). <x-confirm-dialog> asks before actions, hx-confirm requests and data-confirm links and buttons go ahead (see Confirmation), and renders the form <x-row-actions> submits, so row actions need it even without JavaScript. <x-action-run>, inside the toasts, shows the progress of an action run just queued.

docs.title: Buttons and filters
docs.text:
<x-button>

A Bootstrap button with the slot as its label.

Attribute Default Description color primary A Bootstrap colour (secondary, success, danger, …): btn-{color}. type submit The button's type: submit, reset or button. id The button's id. name The button's name, posted with the form when it submits it. onclick A JavaScript onclick handler.

It drops any other attribute, so for hx-*, Alpine or disabled write a <button class="btn …"> yourself.

<x-button>Save</x-button>
<x-button color="secondary" type="button" id="preview">Preview</x-button>

<x-button-container>

Wraps a form's buttons with uniform spacing. It takes no attributes.

<x-button-container>
    <x-button>Save</x-button>
</x-button-container>

<x-module-title>

A muted line of text for page headers, with the slot as its text. It takes no attributes.

<x-module-title>Manage the site's users</x-module-title>

<x-filter-link>

The "Filter" link that shows and hides the filters of a resource list. It takes no attributes and no slot. It toggles an Alpine filtered variable, so put it inside an element with x-data="{filtered: false}". See Filters.

<x-filter-list>

The panel that holds a resource list's filters, shown while filtered is true. It takes no attributes; the slot is the filters, usually the Filters::renderList cell.

<div x-data="{filtered: false}" hx-target="#content-list">
    <x-filter-link />

    <div class="row">
        <div class="col order-2 order-md-1" id="content-list">
            <?= $this->include('Blog\Views\_table') ?>
        </div>

        <x-filter-list>
            <?= view_cell('Bonfire\Core\Cells\Filters::renderList', 'model=PostFilter target=#content-list') ?>
        </x-filter-list>
    </div>
</div>

docs.title: Pager templates
docs.text:
Bonfire registers six pager templates. Name one when you render the links:

<?= $pager->links('default', 'bonfire_list_hx') ?>
Template Renders htmx target bonfire_full First, Previous, two page numbers either side, Next, Last. None (full page loads) bonfire_full_hx The same links, loaded through htmx. #content-list bonfire_simple Newer and Older links. None (full page loads) bonfire_simple_hx Newer and Older links, loaded through htmx. #content-list bonfire_list_hx The admin list footer: "Showing X of Y" with Previous and Next buttons, loaded through htmx. The nearest hx-target ancestor bonfire_head <link rel="prev">, <link rel="canonical"> and <link rel="next"> tags. —

The page-link templates render nothing when there is only one page; bonfire_list_hx still shows its "Showing" line.

bonfire_full_hx and bonfire_simple_hx swap the response into #content-list, so give the element that holds your list that id. bonfire_list_hx sets no target of its own: put hx-target (and any hx-include) on an element that wraps the list, as in the Filters example.

bonfire_head belongs in the page's <head>, so search engines can follow the pages:

<?= $pager->links('default', 'bonfire_head') ?>

The templates are package views in src/Views/, not part of the published theme, so composer update updates them. To change one, register your own template in app/Config/Pager.php and use its name instead.

docs.title: Building Sites
docs.text:
While Bonfire focuses on providing a powerful backend area for your sites, a number of the provided tools can be used within your front-end sites with minimal work. This includes some helper functions for working with dates, a user consent framework for helping you comply with some of the global privacy laws, like GDPR, new tools to build your views with, and more.

Much like any CodeIgniter application, your code will typically live in the /app folder, utilizing the standard Controllers, Models, Views, and other folders for your code. You can, of course, located modules anywhere you wish as long as the autoloader can find it. None of this changes using Bonfire. All of Bonfire's code is kept in the vendor folder, where it will not conflict with your application's code. There are new config files to keep an eye out for.

There is also an example frontpage with a full-blown App theme bonfire2-frontpage-theme for you to look at.
