docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
Bonfire uses Tatter\Alerts to provide support for simple alerts. The usage is simple: 

alert('success', 'Your message goes here.');

This displays a green message that appears in the top-right corner of the admin area. The first argument (success) specifies a Bootstrap alert type that is added to the class automatically to specify how it looks. The second argument is the content that should be in the alert and can be a single string or an array of strings to apply multiple alerts.

Additionally, you can use flash messages in the session to trigger alerts. This would typically be used during a redirect: 

return redirect()->back()->with('message', 'It worked!');
return redirect()->back()->with('error', 'Did not work');
return redirect()->back()->with('error', ['not good', 'nope', 'cannot do it']);

When an array is used it will display a new alert for each element in the array.

You can adjust which session variables are checked and their class mapping using the Alerts config file. Read more in the docs at the repo linked above.

docs.title: Add CSS and JS to Your Site Theme
docs.text: This guide adds your own stylesheet and script to the public site's App theme, with cache-busting handled for you. For every helper argument and config setting, see the Asset Management reference.

docs.title: 1. Put the files in the theme
docs.text:
Save your files inside the App theme folder, for example:

themes/App/css/site.css
themes/App/js/site.js

docs.title: 2. Link them from the layout
docs.text:
The app folder alias points at the App theme, so start each path with app/. Add the links to themes/App/master.php, next to the existing asset_link() calls:

<?= asset_link('app/css/site.css', 'css') ?>
<?= asset_link('app/js/site.js', 'js', 'defer') ?>

Bonfire adds a cache-busting string to each URL, so browsers fetch the new file whenever it changes.

If you need only the URL, for example to write the tag yourself, use asset():

<link rel="stylesheet" href="<?= asset('app/css/site.css', 'css') ?>" />

docs.title: 3. Optional: switch to version-based cache-busting
docs.text:
By default the cache-busting string comes from each file's modified time, which costs a file read per link. On busy sites, set a version instead in app/Config/Assets.php and bump it with each deploy:

public $bustingType = 'version';

public $versions = [
    'css' => '1.1',
    'js'  => '1.1',
];

In the development and testing environments Bonfire uses the current time instead, so nothing is cached while you work.

docs.title: Common functions
docs.text:
Bonfire loads these helpers from src/Common.php on every request, so you can call them anywhere without helper().

Helper Returns app_date() A date formatted with the General Settings date and time formats has_error() Whether a form field has a validation error error() A form field's validation error message render() A view rendered with a given theme admin_accent() The admin theme's accent color site_offline() Whether the site is in maintenance mode

docs.title: app_date()
docs.text:
app_date($date, bool $includeTime = false, bool $includeTimezone = false): string

This helper will display a date based on the current settings in the General Settings page for date format and the application's current timezone. You can pass a string with the date, a DateTime object, or a CodeIgniter\i18n\Time instance as the first argument.

echo app_date('2021-01-15 15:35:00');
// outputs: 01/15/2021

$date = new DateTime('2021-01-15 15:35:00');
echo app_date($date);

$date = new CodeIgniter\i18n\Time('2021-01-15 15:35:00');
echo app_date($date);

You can include the time, formatted as specified in General Settings, by passing true as the second argument.

echo app_date($date, true);
// outputs: 01/15/2021 3:35 PM

You can further include the timezone by passing true as the third argument.

echo app_date($date, true, true);
// outputs: 01/15/2021 3:35 PM CST

docs.title: has_error() and error()
docs.text:
has_error(string $field): bool
error(string $field): string

has_error() returns true when the field has a validation error. error() returns that error's message, or an empty string when there is none.

Both read the errors flash data from the session, so redirect back with the errors under that name:

if (! $this->validate($rules)) {
    return redirect()->back()->withInput()->with('errors', $this->validator->getErrors());
}

withInput() on its own isn't enough. It stores the errors under a different session key, which these helpers don't read.

Then show the error next to the field in the view:

<input type="text" name="policyUrl" class="form-control" value="<?= old('policyUrl') ?>">
<?php if (has_error('policyUrl')) : ?>
    <p class="text-danger small mb-0"><?= error('policyUrl') ?></p>
<?php endif ?>

docs.title: render()
docs.text:
render(string $theme, string $view, array $data = [], array $options = []): string

Renders $view with the theme $theme, where there is no controller to do it, such as in a route closure. It loads the assets helper, makes $theme the current theme, and passes the viewMeta service to the view as $viewMeta. $options goes to CodeIgniter's view renderer, as with view().

$routes->get('admin/blog/preview', static fn () => render('Admin', 'App\Modules\Blog\Views\preview', [
    'title' => 'Preview',
]));

The theme name must match the theme's folder name exactly, including case. See Render without a controller.

docs.title: admin_accent()
docs.text:
admin_accent(): string

Returns the Site.adminAccent setting as a #rrggbb hex string. When the stored value isn't a valid hex color, it returns the default, #D9622B. See Admin accent color.

docs.title: site_offline()
docs.text:
site_offline(): bool

Returns true while the site is in maintenance mode, that is, when the Site.siteOnline setting is empty (false, 0, '0' or null). Use it to show something only while the site is offline:

<?php if (site_offline()) : ?>
    <div class="alert alert-warning">The site is offline. Only staff can see it.</div>
<?php endif ?>

docs.title: Maintenance mode
docs.text:
While the site is offline, only superadmins and users with the site.viewOffline permission can use it. Everyone else is sent to /site-offline, a page that says the site is temporarily offline.

Warning

The login page is offline too, so a superadmin who isn't logged in can't log in to bring the site back. Stay logged in while the site is offline, or see If you're locked out.

docs.title: Take the site offline
docs.text:
In the admin, go to Settings → General and turn off Site Online. While the site is offline, the admin shows a banner with a link back to that setting.

To do it from code, store an empty value in the setting:

setting('Site.siteOnline', false);

docs.title: Let others in
docs.text: Superadmins always get in. To let a group in as well, give it the site.viewOffline permission: tick it on the group's permissions page, or add it to the group in app/Config/AuthGroups.php. See Permissions.

docs.title: Show your own offline page
docs.text:
/site-offline shows the view named in Site::$siteOfflineView. Point it at your own view in app/Config/Site.php:

public $siteOfflineView = 'App\Views\offline';

Visiting /site-offline while the site is online redirects to the home page.

docs.title: Bring the site back online
docs.text:
Turn Site Online back on in Settings → General, or:

setting('Site.siteOnline', true);

docs.title: If you're locked out
docs.text:
When no one who can get in is logged in, delete the stored setting from the database. The site then falls back to Site::$siteOnline in app/Config/Site.php, which is true by default:

DELETE FROM settings WHERE `key` = 'siteOnline';

If you use a table prefix, add it to settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The online filter runs before every request except /site-offline. It calls site_offline(), and when the site is offline, it redirects anyone who isn't a superadmin and doesn't have site.viewOffline. See Request flow for where it runs among Bonfire's other filters, and Configuration Reference for the Site config keys.

docs.title: View Components
docs.text: View Components (or just Components) allow you to create custom HTML elements to use within your views.

docs.title: Self-Closing Tag Components
docs.text:
At their most basic, components serve as dynamic templates that allow you to reduce the typing in your application. This can help boil longer, complex sections down to a single HTML tag. This is especially useful with CSS utility frameworks like TailWind, or when using the utilities in Bootstrap 5, etc. Using components in these situations allows you to keep the style info in one place where making changes to one file changes every instance of the view throughout the application.

To create a component, simply create a new view file within the theme's Components directory, or the application's, app/Views/Components directory.

A simple avatar image might look something like this: 

// app/Views/Components/avatar.php
<img
  src="<?= $src ?? '' ?>"
  class="rounded-circle shadow-4"
  style="width: <?= $width ?? '150px' ?>;"
  alt="<?= $alt ?? '' ?>"
/>

When using the component within a view, you would insert a tag with x- prepended to the filename: 

<x-avatar src="<?= $user->avatarLink() ?>" alt="<?= $user->name ?>" />

Any attributes provided when you insert the component like this are made available as variables within the component view. In this case, the $src and $alt attributes are passed to the component view, resulting in the following output: 

<img
  src="http://example.com/avatars/foo.jpg"
  class="rounded-circle shadow-4"
  style="width: 150px"
  alt="John Smith"
/>

docs.title: Components With Opening and Closing Tags
docs.text:
You can include the content within the opening and closing tags by inserting the reserved $slot variable: 

<x-green-button>Click Me!</x-green-button>

// app/Views/Components/green-button.php
<button class="btn btn-success">
    <?= $slot ?>
</button>

docs.title: Controlled Components
docs.text:
Finally, you can create a class to add additional logic to the output for both self-closing tags and tags with content. The file must be in the same directory as the component view, and should have a name that is the PascalCase version of the filename, with 'Component' added to the end of it. Any attributes that you set on the custom element and any content within element will be passed to the class of the controlled component to be, optionally, processed by the component class and/or rendered by the comonent view file. The data you pass will be available within the class as it's $data property (the tag content – as $data['slot'] property).

A famous-qoutes component would have a view called famous-quotes.php and a controlling class called FamousQuotesComponent.php. The class must extend Bonfire\View\Component. The only requirement is that you implement a method called render().

Below are example files of a usable famous-quotes component, that can be included in any of these three ways:

<x-famous-quotes />
<x-famous-quotes seconds="30" />
<x-famous-quotes seconds="30">Famous Quotes</x-famous-quotes>

It's controlling class file FamousQuotesComponent.php:

namespace App\Components;

/**
 * This example controlled component allows to retrieve a random famous quote
 * from the ZenQuotes API and cache it for a specified number of seconds.
 * Number of seconds can be passed as a parameter to the component.
 * If you want to add a title to the component, you can pass it as a $slot variable.
 */
class FamousQuotesComponent extends \Bonfire\View\Component
{
    protected $defaultNoOfSeconds         = 600;
    protected string $famousQuotesAPINode = 'https://zenquotes.io/api/random';

    public function render(): string
    {
        return $this->renderView($this->view, $this->getFamousQuote());
    }

    public function getFamousQuote(): array
    {
        helper('cache');

        if (isset($this->data['seconds']) && is_numeric($this->data['seconds'])) {
            $this->data['seconds'] = (int) round($this->data['seconds'], 0);
        } else {
            $this->data['seconds'] = $this->defaultNoOfSeconds;
        }

        $cacheKey = 'famous_quote';

        if ($cachedQuote = cache($cacheKey)) {
            return $cachedQuote;
        }

        $response  = file_get_contents($this->famousQuotesAPINode);
        $quoteData = json_decode($response, true);

        if (isset($quoteData[0])) {
            $this->data['quote'] = [
                'text'   => $quoteData[0]['q'],
                'author' => $quoteData[0]['a'],
            ];

            cache()->save($cacheKey, $this->data, $this->data['seconds']);
        } else {
            $this->data['quote'] = [
                'text'   => 'Sucking at something is the first step to becoming sorta good at something.',
                'author' => 'Jake (from "Adventure Time")',
            ];
        }

        return $this->data;
    }
}

And it's view file famous-quotes.php:

<div class="card mb-3">
    <div class="card-header">
        <?= esc($slot ?? '') ?>
    </div>
    <div class="card-body mt-3">
        <p class="card-text text-center"><?= esc($quote['text']) ?></p>
        <footer class="blockquote-footer text-center"><em><?= esc($quote['author']) ?></em></footer>
    </div>
    <div class="card-footer" style="font-size:10px;">Cached for <?= esc($seconds) ?> seconds</div>
</div>

docs.title: Load Analytics Only After Visitors Consent
docs.text: This guide turns on Bonfire's cookie consent form and loads an analytics script only for visitors who accept performance cookies. For every setting and how to customize the form, see the Consent reference.

docs.title: 1. Turn on the consent form
docs.text:
In the admin area, go to Settings → Consent and enable consent. Alternatively, set it in app/Config/Consent.php:

public bool $requireConsent = true;

While consent is off, has_consent() always returns true and no form is shown.

docs.title: 2. Point to your cookie policy
docs.text: On the same settings screen, set the cookie policy URL and title, or set $policyUrl and $policyTitle in the config file. The form links to this page.

docs.title: 3. Wrap the script in a consent check
docs.text:
In your view or layout, wrap the analytics tag in has_consent(), passing the consent's key:

<?php if (has_consent('performance')) : ?>
<script>
    <!-- Global Site Tag (gtag.js) - Google Analytics -->
    ... (several lines of code) ...
</script>
<?php endif ?>

The helper is loaded automatically in controllers that extend Bonfire's BaseController.

Visitors who have not answered, or who rejected performance cookies, no longer load the script. The same check works in controllers, before you set a cookie or call a tracking service.

docs.title: Add a Custom Field to User Profiles
docs.text: This guide stores an extra piece of information on users, a website URL, without changing the users table. For the full set of field options and methods, or to add meta to your own entities, see the Meta Info reference.

docs.title: 1. Define the field
docs.text:
Add the field to $metaFields in app/Config/Users.php. The outer key is the fieldset legend on the user form:

public $metaFields = [
    'Profile' => [
        'website_url' => ['label' => 'Website', 'type' => 'text', 'validation' => 'permit_empty|valid_url_strict'],
    ],
];

The field now appears on the Create/Edit User form in the admin area, and its value is validated and saved with the user.

docs.title: 2. Read the value
docs.text:
$user = model('UserModel')->find(5);

$website = $user->meta('website_url'); // null if not set

docs.title: 3. Write the value from your own forms
docs.text:
saveMeta() saves immediately; there is no need to save the user afterwards:

$user->saveMeta('website_url', $this->request->getPost('website_url'));

To save several fields at once, use syncMeta(). Fields passed with an empty value are deleted, and keys not defined in $metaFields are ignored:

$user->syncMeta([
    'website_url' => 'https://example.com',
]);

docs.title: View Metadata
docs.text:
Bonfire provides a Metadata service that simplifies working with the meta information, scripts, and styles in your application.

$viewMeta = service('viewMeta');

// Add the page title
$viewMeta->setTitle('My Site');

// Add misc page meta data
$viewMeta->addMeta(['description' => 'This is the description of the page']);
$viewMeta->addMeta(['property' => 'og:title', 'content' => 'This is the title of the page']);

// Add link tags
$viewMeta->addLink(['rel' => 'canonical', 'href' => 'https://example.com/']);
$viewMeta->addLink(['rel' => 'icon', 'href' => 'favicon.ico', 'type' => 'image/x-icon']);

// Add script tags
$viewMeta->addScript(['src' => 'https://example.com/js/jquery.min.js']);
$viewMeta->addScript(['src' => 'https://example.com/js/bootstrap.min.js', 'type' => 'text/javascript']);

// Adding script blocks
$script = <<<TEXT
    // all your javscript code here
TEXT;
$viewMeta->addRawScript($script);

The addMeta, addLink and addScript methods all take an array of key value pairs. Each of the pairs will have all of the key/value pairs rendered as key=value within the tags, so you can fully customize what each one contains.

docs.title: Outputting the Metadata
docs.text:
Within your layouts you can use the render() method to render any of the data types.

// Render the title tag - <title>...</title>
<?= $viewMeta->render('title') ?>
// Get just the title value
<?= $viewMeta->title() ?>

// Render all meta tags
<?= $viewMeta->render('meta') ?>

// Render all link tags
<?= $viewMeta->render('link') ?>

// Render all script tags
<?= $viewMeta->render('script') ?>
<?= $viewMeta->render('rawScripts') ?>

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Bonfire provides a simple interface that you can use in place of calling config() to allow you to read and store config values in the database. If the value has not been updated and saved in the database then the original value from the config file will be used.

This allows you to save your application's default state as values in config files, all stored in version control, and still allows your users to override those settings once the site is live.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: A migration is provided that will create the required settings table. It was run during by the Bonfire installation script. No other setup is needed.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
To retrieve a config value use the setting() helper method that is always loaded. Pass the class name and the key joined with a dot:

// The same as config('App')->siteName;
$siteName = setting('App.siteName');
// or
$siteName = setting()->get('App.siteName');

In this case we used the short class name, App, which the config() method automatically locates within the app/Config directory. If it was from a module, it would be found there. Either way, the fully qualified name is automatically detected by the Settings class to keep values separated from config files that may share the same name but different namespaces.

To save a value, call the set() method on the settings class, providing the dotted class name and key, and the value. Note that boolean true/false will be converted to strings :true and :false when stored in the database, but will be converted back into a boolean when retrieved. Arrays and objects are serialized when saved, and unserialized when retrieved. 

setting()->set('App.siteName', 'My Great Site');

docs.title: Admin accent color
docs.text:
The admin theme's highlight color is the Site.adminAccent setting, a #rrggbb hex string that defaults to #D9622B. Admins change it under Settings → General. To set it from code:

setting('Site.adminAccent', '#2F6FEB');

Use the admin_accent() helper to read it. The helper always returns a valid hex color and falls back to the default when the stored value isn't one.

docs.title: Working With AI Agents
docs.text:
AI coding agents don't know Bonfire's conventions. Left alone, they tend to write plain CodeIgniter controllers instead of modules, hand-roll Bootstrap instead of using the admin view components, edit files in vendor/ instead of your published themes and config, and mix in patterns from Bonfire 1 or older CodeIgniter versions.

Bonfire can write a short guide for them into your project's AGENTS.md, the file Cursor, Copilot, Codex and other agents read for project instructions:

php spark bf:agents

The guide says where things live, the rules to follow when adding admin features, and which page of these docs to read for each task. It points to the docs that ship with the package in vendor/lonnieezell/bonfire/docs/, so they always match the version you have installed.

docs.title: Your own text is kept
docs.text:
Bonfire's part of AGENTS.md sits between two markers:

<!-- bonfire:start -->
...
<!-- bonfire:end -->
  • With no AGENTS.md, the command creates one holding just this section.
  • With an AGENTS.md that has no markers, the section is added at the end. Nothing above it changes.
  • With both markers, only the text between them is replaced, so running the command again is safe.

Write your own instructions outside the markers. If the markers are broken (one is missing, they are out of order, or there is more than one pair), the command writes nothing and tells you what is wrong. Fix or remove them by hand and run it again; repairing them automatically could delete your own text.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md rather than AGENTS.md. If your project has a CLAUDE.md, the command reminds you to import the guide from it by adding this line:

@AGENTS.md

The command never edits CLAUDE.md itself.

docs.title: Keeping it up to date
docs.text:
The guide names the Bonfire version it was written for. To refresh it after every update, add the command to the post-update-cmd scripts of your composer.json, next to the breaking changes check:

"scripts": {
    "post-update-cmd": [
        "php spark notify:breaking-changes",
        "php spark bf:agents"
    ]
}

docs.title: Bonfire Application Structure
docs.text: Bonfire is an add-on to CodeIgniter 4, packaged as a set of modules and libraries that can be used together or independently. That means that all of its code lives within the vendor folder, leaving your app folder clean and uncluttered with boilerplate code. But there are a few files and folders that you should be aware of.

docs.title: Config files
docs.text:
Once installed, Bonfire will have copied several configuration files into your app/Config folder. These files are used to configure the various modules and libraries that Bonfire provides. You can modify these files to change the behavior of Bonfire. The following files are copied over:

  • Assets - Used to define how the Assets library should behave.
  • Auth, AuthGroups, AuthTokens - These files are part of the Shield authentication library and are used to define your initial user groups, permissions, and how the authentication system should behave.
  • Bonfire - This allows you to customize some views used by Bonfire, as well as define any additional modules it should know about and load, and allows you to modify the order of the default admin menu items.
  • Site - Allows you to define whether the site is online or in maintenance mode, set the site name, and more.
  • Themes - Determines which themes are available to the system, and some view component settings.
  • Consent - Defines how the Cookie Consent library should behave.
  • Dashboard - Allows you to define the widgets that should be displayed on the dashboard.
  • Recycler - Defines how the Recycler library should behave, and lets an app add or override its resources.
  • Users - Contains avatar settings, custom user fields, and more.

The Configuration Reference lists every key in these files, its default and what it does.

docs.title: /themes
docs.text:
A new folder is created in the project root that holds the view files that define a theme for Bonfire. Themes provide the basic structure of the web pages, including all of the information that surrounds the actual content. By default, it ships with three themes, admin, app, and auth.

  • The admin theme is what is used for the Bonfire admin area.
  • The app theme is extremely simple and is meant mostly as a semi-functional skeleton that you can leverage as a starting point for your app.
  • The auth theme is more a set of partials that are used for all of the authentication-related screens. You can specify which layout it should extend with the layout key of $views in app/Config/Auth.php (see Authentication and Authorization).

docs.title: Change Log
docs.text:
This holds the change history for Bonfire as we lead up to a 1.0 release. It's not exhaustive, but should give you a good idea of the changes that have been made and how it might impact you.

IMPORTANT! Breaking changes are marked with words breaking change in parentheses right after the date.

docs.title: 30 October 2026
docs.text:
New admin guides cover the shipped screens: Users (including Settings → Users), General Settings, Email Settings and Tools (System Info and Logs). Bonfire Modules now lists every shipped module.

A new page, Menus, lists every MenuItem key, the collection and menu methods, custom menus, and reordering with $menuWeights.

The Authentication page now lists Bonfire's defaults for registration, magic links, redirects and the email activation and 2FA actions, and shows where to change each one. It also documents the Auth theme's <x-auth-card> and <x-unsplash> components.

Common functions now covers every helper in src/Common.php: has_error(), error(), render(), admin_accent() and site_offline(), alongside app_date(). A new Maintenance mode section explains how to take the site offline, who can still get in, and how to get back in if you're locked out.

View Components now lists the attributes of every component and has a Pager templates section covering bonfire_full, bonfire_simple, bonfire_list_hx and the rest.

The bonfire_simple pager template no longer prints a stray ?> above its links.

docs.title: 29 October 2026
docs.text:
Four config keys now do what they say. Users::$avatarResizeFloor sets the smallest allowed avatar size, Users::$avatarDirectory also sets where avatar links point, and Users::$avatarNameBasis = 'username' takes an avatar's letters from the username, not the email. Users::$includeMetaFieldsInSearech is now spelled $includeMetaFieldsInSearch; published configs that still use the old spelling keep working. The unused Themes::$haveComponents is gone.

POST admin/settings/groups, without a group alias, now returns 404. It used to throw an ArgumentCountError.

A new page, Configuration Reference, lists every key in the published config files with its default and what it does, including keys that weren't documented before.

The Users sidebar item now needs users.list, the permission the users list page checks, not users.view. The admin and developer groups now see it.

The Users, Email and System Info settings pages now check permissions in the controller, not just in the sidebar. Users without users.settings (Users) or admin.settings (Email, System Info and PHP Info) are sent back to the admin dashboard, even if they type the URL.

A new page, Admin Controllers, Views and Themes, covers AdminController, the render() helper, the master layout's sections, and overriding the published Admin theme.

A module's initFront() now runs on public requests. Bonfire boots once per web request from a new bonfire filter, which runs on every route after the session and admin filters, instead of from the admin filter. Bonfire now caches the modules it finds in Config\Bonfire::$appModules for a minute; run php spark cache:clear to pick up a new module folder straight away. See The Module File.

A new tutorial, Build Your First Admin Module, walks you from an empty folder to a working list screen with a permission, search, filters, global search and the Recycler.

A module can now add its own permissions, and grant them to groups by default, from its Config\Registrar instead of asking you to edit app/Config/AuthGroups.php. The new php spark bonfire:permissions command applies the grants. New installs run it for you; after updating, run php spark bonfire:permissions yourself, and again whenever you add a module. See Permissions.

A Composer package can now add a Bonfire module by listing it in the new Config\Bonfire::$packageModules, from its own Config\Registrar so the app using it changes nothing. See Modules in Composer packages.

The email settings page now saves the SMTP port and timeout as integers. Sending SMTP mail no longer fails with a fsockopen() TypeError, and port 465 turns on implicit SSL again. A custom port must now be a positive number. Thanks to Alistair Wearring for the report and fix.

Resource tabs added with service('resourceTabs')->addTabFor() are now shown as the current tab on their own page. On group pages, (id) in a tab's URL is now replaced with the group's alias instead of being left in the link. The Resource Tabs page now shows how to build the page a tab links to.

ComponentRenderer::render(null) now returns an empty string instead of throwing a TypeError. Text like <x- /> is left alone instead of failing the page with "View not found for component". Paired components with one- or two-letter names (<x-em>…</x-em>) now render, and a closing tag that doesn't match its opening tag's name is left alone rather than rendering a shorter-named component. A > inside a quoted attribute of a paired component (<x-foo title="a>b">…</x-foo>) no longer cuts the attribute short.

A new php spark bf:agents command writes a guide to Bonfire's conventions for AI coding agents into your project's AGENTS.md: where things live, the rules for admin modules, and which docs page to read for each task. Your own text in that file is kept, and running it again only replaces Bonfire's section. Add it to the post-update-cmd scripts of your composer.json to keep the guide in step with the installed version. See Working With AI Agents.

A Recycler dashboard widget (recycler:summary) shows how many deleted records each Recycler resource holds, leaving out those with none, and links each to its list in the Recycler. Resources other modules register with service('recycler') appear in it without extra setup. It needs the recycler.view permission; add it from Add widget on the dashboard. The existing "Users in Recycler" stat stays, since saved layouts use it.

A System health dashboard widget (tools:systemHealth) lists problems with the install: each file or folder in writable/ that can't be written to, a missing .env file, and server load above a limit you set (default 4). When there are none it says so, and it links to the System Info page. It needs the admin.settings permission; add it from Add widget on the dashboard. The checks moved into Bonfire\Tools\Libraries\SystemHealth, which System Info now uses too.

An Action runs dashboard widget (actions:runs) lists your own queued, running and recently failed bulk action runs, newest first, each linking to its progress. Settings choose how many to show, how many days of ended runs to include and whether completed runs appear. It needs no permission; add it from Add widget on the dashboard. Opening a run's progress link (action-run) directly now shows it inside the admin page rather than as a bare fragment. ActionRunModel now returns created_at and updated_at as CodeIgniter\I18n\Time rather than strings.

A Recently active dashboard widget (users:recentlyActive) lists the users active within the last 5 minutes, hour or 24 hours, most recent first, each linking to their account. It needs the users.list permission; add it from Add widget on the dashboard.

A Recent failed logins dashboard widget (users:failedLogins) lists the newest unsuccessful login attempts across all accounts, with the identifier, IP address and date. Attempts by a known user's email link to their Security tab for admins who may open it. It needs the users.view permission; add it from Add widget on the dashboard.

docs.title: 29 October 2026 (breaking change)
docs.text:
An action run's lifecycle now lives in service('actionRuns') (Bonfire\Actions\ActionRuns): dispatch() runs an action in the request or queues it, process() runs a queued run, and progress() and toast() look one up for the admin who started it. ActionRunModel now reads and writes status as a Bonfire\Actions\RunStatus enum in place of the strings queued, running, done and failed, so code that writes a status string to it must pass the enum. The Admin theme's <x-action-run> now calls service('actionRuns')->toast() rather than ActionRunModel; installs that published the Admin theme should copy the new themes/Admin/Components/action-run.php.

Picking an accent color swatch under Settings → General → Appearance now shows the save bar, so the new color can be saved. Before, only the color picker itself did.

docs.title: 28 October 2026
docs.text:
spark notify:breaking-changes used to keep its marker in a last-update.txt file inside the package folder, which composer update deleted together with the previous version, so it warned on every update. It now remembers the breaking change it last reported in writable/bonfire-breaking-changes.json: expect one more warning after this update, and none for changes you have already been shown.

The check also notices a note added to an existing (breaking change) heading, not only a new heading, and a fresh install no longer warns about changes that came before it. If writable/ is recreated on every deploy, move the marker with Config\Bonfire::$breakingChangeStateFile. See Updating Bonfire.

The dashboard's widget library now lists widgets by the module that adds them, in name order, in place of by type. A widget's group() gives its module's name; the type keys quickLinks, stats, charts and custom still work, each under its own heading. A StatsItem or ChartsItem takes 'module' => '…' (see Dashboard Widgets). With the library open, the page now widens by its width instead of narrowing the dashboard, where the screen has room.

The sidebar now shows Settings as a single link to the first settings page you may open, since the settings pages list one another in their own nav. A menu collection opts into this with setPageNav(). Installs that published the Admin theme keep the old expanding Settings menu until they copy the new themes/Admin/Components/sidebar.php.

Each admin can now change a dashboard widget's settings for their own dashboard: in edit mode, its sliders button opens them in a panel, and they are saved with the layout (see The Dashboard). Stat cards, charts and Log activity have settings; until an admin changes one, it follows the site-wide value in Settings → Widgets. Widgets declare their settings with fields(), a list of Bonfire\Dashboard\WidgetField, and get their values in render(WidgetValues $values); DashboardWidget::settingsUrl() is gone (see Dashboard Widgets).

The Log activity widget now shows a column for each of the last days up to today, with a thin line for days without a log file. Its Days to show setting (formerly Log files to show) keeps its saved value, and now defaults to 7.

Dashboard widgets can need a permission: pass 'permission' to a StatsItem or ChartsItem, and admins who lack it don't see it in the widget library or on their dashboard, nor is its data fetched for them. The built-in Users widgets need users.list and the Groups widgets groups.settings. Admins with widgets.settings can Save as site default from the dashboard's edit bar, and Reset site default in Settings → Widgets (see The Dashboard). The Settings → Widgets switches are now labelled as choosing which widgets are available. Quick Links is now a native widget, Bonfire\Dashboard\Widgets\QuickLinksWidget, registered by the Dashboard module under its old id, and no longer in the default Dashboard.cells; installs that still list Bonfire\Dashboard\DashboardCells::quickLinks show it once, in place. DashboardCells::quickLinks() is deprecated. Building widgets is documented in Dashboard Widgets.

docs.title: 28 October 2026 (breaking change)
docs.text:
StatsItem::addValue(), addValueByFreeQuery() and ChartsItem::addDataset() now store their query and run it when the item's value or data is first read, which the dashboard does only for the widgets it shows. They keep their signatures. service('dashboardContext'), Bonfire\Widgets\DashboardContext, LayoutResolver::includes() and CellWidget::aliasOf() are gone: a value you build by hand belongs in a widget's render() (see Dashboard Widgets), which the dashboard calls only for a widget that is placed and permitted. A view that still calls the WidgetCells::stats or ::charts cell directly now runs the query of every item it lists. Tests that injected a DashboardContext mock no longer need one.

Settings → Widgets is gone. Permissions decide who may see a widget, and each admin's settings for a placed widget decide how it looks, so the page's switches and defaults repeated them. Every widget is now offered to anyone who holds its permission(): a widget switched off there is offered again. A placed widget follows its fields' coded default until the admin changes a setting, so a site-wide default saved there, such as a chart's color scheme, no longer applies. Run php spark migrate --all: a migration forgets those stored values. Delete any published copy of the removed Config classes below (such as app/Config/Stats.php), which extends a class that is gone. This replaces what the notes below say about Settings → Widgets. Reset site default has moved into the dashboard's edit bar, next to Save as site default, for admins with widgets.settings (see The Dashboard). Code that used the removed API: WidgetField's factories no longer take key: (a key passed by position now lands in description), and WidgetField::inherited() is gone (read default); Bonfire\Widgets\WidgetOptions and the Bonfire\Widgets\Config\Stats, LineChart, BarChart, DoughnutChart, PieChart, PolarAreaChart and LogActivity classes are gone; ItemSettings keeps only widgetId(); and ItemWidget::available() is gone. The widgets-settings and widgets-reset-layout routes are gone; the reset is now dashboard-site-layout-reset.

The five User classification by group charts (line, bar, doughnut, pie and polar area) are gone: Users by group shows the same numbers. Saved dashboards that placed one lose it: add Users by group from the widget library. The User Groups stat card stays. ChartsItem is unchanged, so modules can still add charts of their own.

Log activity is now a dashboard widget of its own, Bonfire\Tools\Widgets\LogActivity, like Recent errors. It keeps its id logs:logActivity, so saved layouts keep it in place, and its days and Debug defaults in Settings → Widgets keep their saved values. It no longer has a switch under Available widgets: every admin with logs.view can add it, even where it was switched off. It is no longer an item of service('widgets')->widget('logs'), so the Bonfire\Widgets\Cells\WidgetCells::logs cell no longer shows it. Code that calls it directly: days() and levels() now take the options as arguments, days(int $count, bool $hideDebug) and levels(bool $hideDebug); render() takes a WidgetValues; and setTitle(), withOptions(), module() and settings() are gone.

List rows are now selectable whenever the admin may run any of the list's bulk actions, not only when they may delete: a module's bulk action shows the checkboxes on its own. A row's checkbox is disabled when no bulk action allows() that record. ActionList::selectable() answers both, and ActionList::showing() hands a page's records to <x-row-actions>, which no longer loads its record with one query per row once the view calling it does so. Installs that published the Admin theme should copy the new themes/Admin/Components/row-actions.php, themes/Admin/Search/users.php and themes/Admin/_table_head.php; _table_head.php now shows the select-all checkbox only when $showSelectAll is true, rather than whenever it is set and the admin has users.delete.

Each widget's fields() is now the only place its settings are declared: the Settings → Widgets tabs are built from the fields that have a key, one tab per settings class, and saved through them. Values you saved there keep working. The properties of Bonfire\Widgets\Config\Stats, LineChart, BarChart, DoughnutChart, PieChart, PolarAreaChart and LogActivity are gone, so a default overridden in a published copy of those classes or in .env no longer applies: set it in Settings → Widgets instead. The line chart's subtitle and custom border settings, which had no form, are no longer read. WidgetOptions keeps only all(), forAlias(), save() and reset().

Users by group is now a bar list: each group, a bar scaled to the largest one, and its number of users, with a setting to sort by count or by name. It is a new widget, users:byGroup, in place of the Users by Group stat card (stats:usersExpTable693), which is gone. Saved dashboards that placed the stat card lose it: re-add Users by group from the widget library. Two new widgets: Newest users (the latest users to join, linking to each; needs users.list) and Recent errors (the newest errors, or errors and warnings, across the log files, linking to each log file; needs logs.view). The default dashboard now has Users by group and Newest users in its Users section, in place of the Users in Recycler stat, and Log activity and Recent errors side by side in Monitoring (see The Dashboard). Installs that published the Admin theme need the new .bf-list-card, .bf-bars and .bf-rows rules of themes/Admin/css/admin.css.

Lists have a shared system for row and bulk actions (see Row and Bulk Actions): an action is one class, registered on a named list, run through POST admin/actions/{list}/{action} with permission, CSRF and per-record checks, confirmation (with or without JavaScript), and an optional queue through codeigniter4/queue. Run php spark migrate --all for its new action_runs table. The Users and Logs deletes use it, which removes routes: GET admin/users/{id}/delete and POST admin/users/delete-batch are gone, as is UserController::delete() and deleteBatch(). Links or forms that used them must post to admin/actions/users/delete-users instead, with the IDs in selects[]. The Users and Logs list checkboxes are now named selects[] with the ID as their value. Every inline confirm() is replaced by <x-confirm-dialog>, which also handles hx-confirm. Installs that published their own copy of the Admin theme must re-publish it: master.php gains <x-confirm-dialog /> and <x-action-run />, and the lists use the new <x-row-actions> and <x-bulk-actions>.

<x-switch> gained an offValue attribute: the value its hidden input posts when the switch is off (0 by default). An empty offValue posts nothing, which Bonfire's own views now use for array names like permissions[]. Installs that published their own copy of the Admin theme must re-publish it; an older copy posts 0 for every switch that is off in those lists. The user edit screens (details, permissions and security) use the new admin layout.

The settings pages share a new <x-settings-layout> component (the Settings head and a sub-nav of the settings pages). An older published copy of the Admin theme doesn't have it, so re-publish the theme or those pages fail to render. Turning Site Online off now saves 0; the offline check treats any empty value as offline.

The Logs, log view, Recycler and System Info pages use the new admin layout, with styles an older published copy of the Admin theme doesn't have, so re-publish the theme. A log file can now be downloaded from its page.

A new Log activity dashboard widget charts the entries of the newest log files per level (see The Dashboard). Turn it on in Settings → Widgets; its own tab sets how many files it shows and whether Debug entries are left out. It is shown by a new Bonfire\Widgets\Cells\WidgetCells::logs cell: installs with their own Config\Dashboard must add that cell to $cells to see it. Its styles are in the Admin theme, so re-publish the theme.

Each admin can customize their own dashboard (see The Dashboard): Customize lets them drag widgets into a new order, group them into titled sections, size them (¼ / ⅓ / ½ / ⅔ / Full, from their tools or by dragging a corner), remove them and add others from a widget library, all of it also from the keyboard, with undo and redo. Save layout stores the layout as theirs alone; saving the default layout, after resetting to it, forgets theirs. Every stat card, chart, Log activity and custom cell in Dashboard.cells is now one widget, and modules can add their own by implementing Bonfire\Dashboard\DashboardWidget and calling service('dashboard')->register() in initAdmin() (see Dashboard Widgets). The switches in Settings → Widgets now decide which widgets are available in the palette, and are on unless a site admin switches them off; their stored keys are unchanged. The default dashboard is the new Dashboard.layout config property: Quick Links, a Users section (Users by Group and Users in Recycler) and a Monitoring section (Log activity). Stats, charts and Log activity no longer appear on it by being switched on, and each admin adds the ones they want from the widget library. Installs with their own Config\Dashboard and no $layout property get the plain cells of Dashboard.cells (Quick Links and your own cells) instead. A stats or chart item now fetches its data only when it is on the viewer's dashboard, so service('dashboardContext')->shows() answers "is it in the viewer's layout". The dashboard needs the new admin/js/dashboard.js and new admin.css rules from the Admin theme, so installs that published their own copy of the Admin theme must re-publish it; with an older copy the dashboard shows its widgets stacked in one column and Customize does nothing.

Also fixed: a custom SMTP port is saved and shown again, and a user's name, profile fields and avatar initials are escaped wherever the admin shows them. The Recycler's Restore button no longer asks for confirmation; Purge asks first.

docs.title: 27 October 2026 (breaking change)
docs.text:
The Admin theme is being redesigned. Installs that published their own copy of the Admin theme must re-publish it: Bonfire's admin views now use new View Components (<x-setting-row>, <x-switch>, <x-segmented>, <x-chip>, <x-status>, <x-empty-state>, <x-selection-bar>, <x-tabs>, <x-save-bar>) that an older copy doesn't have, and the shell (master.php, _header.php, Components/sidebar.php) has a new layout. <x-page-head> and <x-admin-box> gained optional attributes and keep working as before without them; <x-button> no longer adds btn-lg. Escape component attribute values with esc(): the renderer now decodes HTML entities in attribute values before handing them to the component, so a custom component that prints an attribute must escape it. See View Components.

Dashboard stats widgets are now neutral cards, so a StatsItem's bgColor no longer has a visible effect.

The admin shell has a collapsible sidebar (remembered per viewer), a breadcrumb, a dark-mode toggle and a ⌘K / Ctrl+K command palette that jumps to any admin page or runs a search. Admin pages below a menu item can name themselves in the breadcrumb with a crumb view section (and crumbParent, when the page isn't under the active menu item).

The admin theme has an accent color. Change it under Settings → General → Appearance, or set it from code with setting('Site.adminAccent', '#2F6FEB'). It must be a #rrggbb hex color. Buttons, links, focus rings and checked inputs follow it. The admin also gains a dark mode that follows the operating system until a viewer picks one, and it now uses the Geist font. Installs that published their own copy of the Admin theme need to re-publish it to get the new tokens; until then the accent setting saves but has no visible effect.

docs.title: 11 October 2026 (breaking change)
docs.text:
Bonfire no longer adds a users rule group to Config\Validation. Nothing in Bonfire used it, and because Config\Validation does not declare $users, it raised a "Creation of dynamic property" deprecation under PHP 8.2+. The rules for the user form live in Bonfire\Users\Config\Users::$validation. If your app calls $this->validate('users'), add the rules you need to your own app/Config/Validation.php as public array $users. If you already declare $users there, Bonfire no longer merges its email, username, first_name and last_name rules into it, so add any of those you rely on.

Fixes: Bonfire found no themes under CodeIgniter 4.7.5, so every admin and auth page failed with "Admin is not a valid theme folder". Theme::available() now lists theme folders itself instead of using get_dir_file_info(), which no longer returns folders.

docs.title: 8 October 2026 (breaking change)
docs.text:
The Recycler no longer guesses at what a model can do by checking method_exists(). A model that customizes the Recycler must now implement the matching interface from Bonfire\Recycler\Interfaces: CustomRecyclerQuery (setupRecycler(): Model), CustomRecyclerRestore (recyclerRestore(int $id): bool) and CustomRecyclerPurge (recyclerPurge(int $id): bool). Methods with those names on a model that does not implement the interface are no longer called. Without a custom hook, the Recycler now uses the model's own primary key and soft delete field instead of assuming id and deleted_at, and refuses to restore or purge a record that is not in the Recycler.

Modules now register their recyclable resources with service('recycler')->register() from initAdmin(), instead of editing Config\Recycler::$resources. The Users module registers users this way, so $resources is empty by default; entries you already have in your own Config\Recycler keep working and take precedence over a module's. If you publish the Recycler listResource view, it now receives RecyclableResource objects as $resources and $currentResource (use ->label(), ->columns(), ->localizedColumns(), ->alias()) and no longer receives $currentAlias.

The logs in the Tools area are now read and deleted through Bonfire\Tools\Libraries\LogStore, which only accepts file names like log-2024-01-31. Logs::getAdjacentLogFiles() moved to LogStore::neighbours() and Logs::paginateLogs() takes the page as its third argument instead of reading $_GET. If you publish the logs list view, each log now has a name (without extension) instead of a filename.

Fixes: viewing and deleting logs now requires the logs.view and logs.manage permissions; before, any user with admin.access could read and delete the logs by calling the URLs directly. "Delete all" now removes only the log files. The levels count in the logs list counts entries instead of every occurrence of a level's name in a message.

View Components now render self-closing (<x-foo />) and paired (<x-foo>…</x-foo>) tags through the same code, so the two forms no longer differ by accident. Two behaviours change:

  • A self-closing tag now passes its attributes to a component class, as the docs always said. Before, <x-foo attr="bar" /> lost attr whenever a FooComponent class existed, so the class' $this->data was empty. If your class worked around that, it now receives the attributes.
  • A tag whose view can't be found now always throws a RuntimeException (View not found for component: foo). Before, a paired tag with a missing view (or any error while rendering one) was swallowed and the raw <x-foo> tag stayed in the page. A regex failure while rendering components also throws now, instead of returning a number as the page.

What a component view sees (the attributes as variables, $slot), the lookup order (theme first, then componentsLookupPaths) and the Components/<name>.php + <Name>Component.php convention are unchanged.

docs.title: 8 October 2026 (breaking change)
docs.text:
Everything about whether a dashboard widget is enabled, and what its display options are, now has one owner in Bonfire\Widgets: ItemSettings (the enabled flag of an item), DashboardContext (are we on the dashboard, and does this item show) and WidgetOptions (the options of the Stats widget and of each chart type). The settings keys stored in your database are unchanged.

If you publish your own copy of the dashboard cell views (Cells/stats.php, Cells/charts.php, Cells/scripts.php) or the widgets settings.php view, note that they no longer receive $manager from Manager::manager(), which has been replaced by Manager::items(). Ask each item for $item->settings()->enabled() instead.

Widget items now also report an item's settings through settings(), which is part of the Item interface. If you wrote your own item class implementing Bonfire\Widgets\Interfaces\Item, add settings(): ItemSettings to it. The protected $dashboardRoute property of StatsItem and ChartsItem is gone. StatsItem::addValue(), addValueByFreeQuery() and ChartsItem::addDataset() still only run their query on the dashboard when the item is enabled, and the check can now be swapped in tests through service('dashboardContext').

Items in a second collection of a widget now show up on the widgets settings page and on the dashboard.

docs.title: 8 October 2026
docs.text:
The rules for who may edit, ban, delete or assign groups and permissions to whom in the Users admin now live in one place (Bonfire\Users\Libraries\UserAccess), and the views and the controller both use it. If you have published your own copy of the Users views form.php, permissions.php or _table.php, they now receive an $access variable (a UserAccess instance) instead of working out these rules themselves. Avatar storage moved to AvatarStorage.

Fixes: purging several users at once now removes the avatar and meta info of every purged user, not only the first. A user with users.edit but without me.edit can no longer ban themselves.

docs.title: 18 March 2025 (breaking change)
docs.text:
The way widgets are enabled has changed in the database, so if you had widgets enabled before, they will all be disabled. To clear the database of the orphaned data about enabled widgets run this in your DB:

DELETE FROM `settings`
WHERE `class` = 'Bonfire\Widgets\Config\Stats' AND `key` LIKE 'Stats_%';
DELETE FROM `settings`
WHERE `class` = 'Bonfire\Widgets\Config\Stats' AND `key` LIKE 'Charts_%';

docs.title: 26 February 2025 (breaking change)
docs.text: Finished implementation of <x-button> component in the Admin theme. Users need to update the Admin theme (updated the component definition).

docs.title: 19 January 2025
docs.text: Resource Meta Info (if you have configured such) can now be included in the Admin area search (see docs page Search for details).

docs.title: 18 January 2025 (breaking change)
docs.text:
Possibility to have Second Factor Authentication is added to Bonfire2, implementing Codeigniter Shield feature.

To use the feature on existing installs you will first need to update the userspace Config file app/Config/Auth.php, in particular – the property $views, two keys relating to 2FA to look like this:

    'action_email_2fa'        => '\Bonfire\Views\Auth\email_2fa_show',
    'action_email_2fa_verify' => '\Bonfire\Views\Auth\email_2fa_verify',

Failing to do that and enabling 2FA in the admin area will lock the users out of your website.

To fix it, after modifying the config file, issue this command on your database to clean up references to wrong classes:

DELETE FROM settings WHERE class="Config\Auth" AND key="actions";

docs.title: 16 January 2025
docs.text:
Bonfire can henceforth warn you about breaking changes (like need to update Admin/Auth themes, change config files, etc).

To get such notifications when updating Bonfire, you can add a command to your composer.json scripts section:

    "scripts": {
        "post-update-cmd": [
            "php spark notify:breaking-changes"
        ]
    }

New Bonfire install will automatically include this command.

docs.title: 18 March 2024 (breaking change)
docs.text:
<x-button> and <x-button-container> view components implemented.

When updating, copy files themes/Admin/Components/button-container.php and themes/Admin/Components/button.php into the corresponding folder of your project's Admin theme. See #434 for details about the change.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: php spark bf:install publishes a copy of each of these config classes to app/Config/, where you edit them. This page lists every key, its default and what it does.

docs.title: Config files or the admin
docs.text: Keys marked Admin can also be changed in the admin under Settings. Bonfire reads them with setting(), which returns the value saved in the database before the value in the config file. Once an admin has saved one, editing the file has no effect until the stored value is removed with setting()->forget(). See Settings.

docs.title: Bonfire
docs.text:
app/Config/Bonfire.php tells Bonfire where to find modules and how to order the admin menu.

Key Default Effect $views ['filter_list' => 'Bonfire\Views\_filter_list'] Views Bonfire renders that you can replace. filter_list is the filter panel of admin lists (see Filters). $appModules [] Folders of app modules, as namespace ⇒ path. Bonfire loads every folder in each path as a module. See Configuring Module Locations. $packageModules [] Single modules in Composer packages, as namespace ⇒ the folder that holds Module.php. See Modules in Composer packages. $menuWeights [] Admin menu order, as named route ⇒ weight. Larger weights appear later. An item that isn't listed keeps the weight its module gives it. Orders the Users menu, app module menus and the items inside Tools and Settings, but not Tools and Settings themselves. $breakingChangeStateFile null Where spark notify:breaking-changes records the last breaking change it reported. null means writable/bonfire-breaking-changes.json. See Updating Bonfire.

An example of $menuWeights:

public $menuWeights = [
    'user-list'   => 1,
    'custom-list' => 2,
    'recycler'    => 1,
    'sys-info'    => 2,
];

docs.title: Site
docs.text:
app/Config/Site.php holds site-wide values.

Key Default Effect $perPage 15 Items per page in admin lists such as Users, the Recycler and the logs. $siteName 'Bonfire' The site name, shown in the admin and used as the default page title. Admin $siteOnline true When false, visitors are redirected to /site-offline. Only superadmins and groups with the site.viewOffline permission can still use the site. Admin $siteOfflineView 'Bonfire\Views\site_offline' The view /site-offline shows while the site is offline. $adminAccent '#D9622B' The admin theme's highlight color, as a #rrggbb hex string. See Admin accent color. Admin

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
app/Config/Themes.php says where themes and view components live. It isn't a BaseConfig, so setting() doesn't apply to it.

Key Default Effect $collections [__DIR__ . '/../../themes/'] Folders that hold themes. Each theme is a direct child folder of a collection. $componentsLookupPaths [APPPATH . 'Views/Components/'] Fallback folders for a view component that the current theme doesn't define, checked in order. Each path must end with /. Use it for a component library shared by several themes.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
app/Config/Users.php covers avatars, the user form and extra user fields.

Key Default Effect $useGravatar false Use gravatar.com for users who haven't uploaded an avatar. Admin $gravatarDefault 'blank' The Gravatar image for emails with no Gravatar: mp, identicon, monsterid, wavatar, retro, robohash or blank. Admin $avatarNameBasis 'name' What the letters on a generated avatar come from: 'name' (initials, or the username when there's no first name) or 'username'. Admin $avatarPalette 11 hex colors Background colors for generated avatars. Each user always gets the same one. $avatarDirectory 'uploads/avatars' Where uploaded avatars are saved and linked from, relative to FCPATH. $avatarResize false Shrink uploaded avatars that are larger than $avatarSize. Admin $avatarSize 140 The largest width or height in pixels of a resized avatar. Admin $avatarResizeFloor 32 The smallest $avatarSize allowed. $validation rules for id, email, username, first_name, last_name, groups.* Validation rules for saving a user in the admin. Rules for the fields in $metaFields are added to them. $metaFields one example field, blog Extra fields on a user's profile, grouped by fieldset legend. See Defining Meta Fields. $includeMetaFieldsInSearch ['blog'] Names of $metaFields fields that the admin search looks in. Older published configs spell it $includeMetaFieldsInSearech, which still works.

docs.title: Consent
docs.text:
app/Config/Consent.php controls the cookie consent banner. The Consent page describes each key in more detail. All keys except the three views can be changed under Settings → Consent.

Key Default Effect $requireConsent false Ask front-end visitors to opt in to each consent type. When false, no banner shows and the consent helper always returns true. Admin $consentLength 180 Days before a visitor is asked again. Admin $consentForm 'Bonfire\Consent\Views\consent_form' The view of the consent banner. $consentFormStyles 'Bonfire\Consent\Views\consent_styles' The view with the banner's CSS, added to each page. $consentFormScripts 'Bonfire\Consent\Views\consent_scripts' The view with the banner's JavaScript, added to each page. $policyUrl 'privacy' The URL of your cookie policy, full or relative. Admin $policyTitle 'Cookie Policy' The link text of the cookie policy link, which replaces {policy_url} in $consentMessage. Admin $consentMessage a short cookie notice The message at the top of the banner. Admin $consents required, performance, targeting The consent types visitors accept or reject, keyed by alias, each with a name and desc. Admin

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
app/Config/Dashboard.php sets the dashboard everyone sees until they customize it.

Key Default Effect $layout quick links, a Users section, a Monitoring section The site default layout. See Setting it in config. A default saved from the dashboard replaces it. $cells Bonfire's stats, logs and charts cells Legacy view cells, shown in order only when $layout is null. See Legacy: view cells.

docs.title: Recycler
docs.text:
app/Config/Recycler.php sets up the Recycler. See The Recycler.

Key Default Effect $defaultResource 'users' The alias of the resource the Recycler opens on. $resources [] Resources registered by the app, keyed by alias, each with a label, model and columns. An entry with a module's alias replaces how that module's resource is shown.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text:
app/Config/Assets.php controls asset URLs and cache busting. The Asset Management page describes each key in more detail.

Key Default Effect $bustingType 'file' How the cache-busting string is made: 'file' uses the file's modified time, 'version' uses $versions in production and the current time elsewhere. $separator '~~' The URL-safe characters put between the file name and the cache-busting string. Must not occur in your asset file names. $versions ['css' => '1.0', 'js' => '1.0'] Versions used when $bustingType is 'version'. $folders app, admin, auth themes and other ⇒ VENDORPATH Folders that can serve assets, keyed by the first segment of the asset URL.

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
app/Config/Alerts.php extends the config of Tatter\Alerts, which has the remaining keys. See Alerts.

Key Default Effect $template 'Bonfire\Views\_alerts.php' The view that renders alerts. $classes Bootstrap types, log levels, messages and errors Session keys that show as alerts, each mapped to the Bootstrap alert class it uses.

docs.title: Auth, AuthGroups and AuthToken
docs.text: These three files configure Shield, which handles login, groups and permissions. Shield's documentation covers their keys. This section lists only what Bonfire adds or changes.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Key Bonfire's default Effect $views Bonfire's views Bonfire's views replace Shield's for login, register, email 2FA, email activation and magic links. layout is the layout of the auth theme they extend, master. email_layout is Bonfire's addition: the layout the magic link email extends. See Views. $actions ['register' => null, 'login' => null] Set them to Bonfire's Bonfire\Auth\Actions\EmailActivator and Bonfire\Auth\Actions\Email2FA, which use Bonfire's views. Admin $sessionConfig 'field' => 'logged_in' Bonfire stores the logged-in user under the logged_in session key, where Shield uses user. allowRemembering and rememberLength are Admin. $personalFields ['first_name', 'last_name'] User fields that a password may not resemble. $userProvider Bonfire\Users\Models\UserModel Bonfire's user model.

$allowRegistration, $minimumPasswordLength and $passwordValidators can also be changed under Settings → Users.

Bonfire also changes loginRedirect(): users with the admin.access permission go to the admin area after login, whatever $redirects['login'] says.

docs.title: AuthGroups
docs.text: Key Bonfire's default Effect $groups, $permissions, $matrix Bonfire's groups and permissions See Bonfire's groups and permissions. Once an admin edits a group's permissions, the matrix is stored in the database and $matrix is ignored. $defaultGroup 'user' The group new users join. Admin $moduleGrants [] Bonfire's addition: permissions modules grant to groups by default. See Default grants.

docs.title: AuthToken
docs.text: Bonfire changes nothing; every key is Shield's.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Bonfire is a set of modules and libraries for CodeIgniter 4. It is designed to be installed via Composer and is not intended to be installed manually. These directions assume that you have Composer installed globally. If you do not, then you will need to adjust the commands according to your setup.

docs.title: Install CodeIgniter App Starter
docs.text:
You must have an existing CodeIgniter 4 project already setup. If you do not already, you can install a new project as detailed in CodeIgniter User Guide by typing the following at the command line:

composer create-project codeigniter4/appstarter my-app
cd my-app

You need to allow installation of development stability level packages by executing the following commands:

composer config minimum-stability dev
composer config prefer-stable true

docs.title: Install Bonfire
docs.text:
Next you need to install Bonfire as a dependency in your project. From your command line type the following (omit :dev-develop if you want the current stable version):

composer require lonnieezell/bonfire:dev-develop

This will download the latest version and all dependencies.

docs.title: Run The Install Script
docs.text:
To setup the initial environment, a CLI command is provided to do all of the setup you need to get up and running. From the project root, type:

php spark bf:install

This will:

  • Copy the env file to .env to save your site's customized setting.
  • Set the environment to development so you can see errors and use the Debug Toolbar
  • Prompt you for your site's base url and update the .env file (i.e. http://localhost:8080 or http://bonfire.test)
  • Remove the index.php from your urls
  • Prompt you for your database credentials and database name, saving that to the .env file
  • Copy all of the Bonfire module config files into your app/Config directory.
  • Copy the theme directories to ROOTPATH/themes

Then it will present you with a recommendation on creating the database via command

php spark db:create <database name>

and to create the initial user via command

php spark bf:install --continue

Continuing the installation will then do the following:

  • Run all migrations so the database is setup and ready to go
  • Prompt you for your super admin name and credentials and create that user in the database.

Info

For getting a feel of Bonfire or even light use websites you can use SQLite3 database engine, which keeps the database in a file and does not require setup.

docs.title: Run the Site
docs.text:
You can now run the site using CodeIgniter's built-in development server:

php spark serve

docs.title: Enjoy!
docs.text:
That's all that's needed to get started. You can now visit http://localhost:8080/admin and login with your new user.

If you'd rather use a different server, like Apache or Nginx, you can follow the CodeIgniter 4 User Guide suggestions for a number of different server setups.

docs.title: Updating Bonfire
docs.text:
After composer update, Bonfire reads the changelog of the version you now have and, when a release since your last update contains breaking changes, prints a warning:

======= WARNING: =======
Breaking changes since the previous update of your Bonfire install detected.
You may need to update your app manually.
Please read the changelog for more information:
vendor/lonnieezell/bonfire/docs/intro/changelog.md
Latest breaking change date: 2026-10-28

The warning is a reminder to read the changelog, nothing more: re-publishing a theme, copying a view or changing a config file is not something an update can do for you. Why Themes Are Published Into Your App explains why.

Bonfire remembers the change it has shown you in writable/bonfire-breaking-changes.json. That folder has to be writable, and it has to survive a deploy, otherwise the same warning comes back after every update. If your server recreates writable/ on each release, point the marker somewhere else in app/Config/Bonfire.php:

public $breakingChangeStateFile = ROOTPATH . 'bonfire-breaking-changes.json';

To turn the check off, remove php spark notify:breaking-changes from the post-update-cmd scripts of your composer.json.

If you use AI coding agents, php spark bf:agents writes Bonfire's conventions into your project's AGENTS.md. Add it to the same post-update-cmd scripts to keep that guide in step with the installed version. See Working With AI Agents.

docs.title: Generate some data for testing
docs.text:
You can insert some records of users into your database by running this migration (each run will add 100 users randomly distributed through Users, Developers and Beta groups, randomly activated):

php spark db:seed Bonfire\\Users\\Database\\Seeds\\Seed100Users

docs.title: Our Philosophy
docs.text:
We believe that the best tools don't get in your way. They don't fight you, or make you jump through hoops to get your work done. But they also don't do everything for you. They provide a solid foundation, and then get out of the way.

We believe that a product can only be as easy to use as its documentation. If you can't figure out how to use it, then it's not a good tool.

We also know that we don't have all the answers. We don't know your specific needs, or the best way to solve your problems. Therefore the tool should be flexible enough to allow you to solve your problems in the way that makes the most sense to you.

We believe we're going to get it wrong along the way. Paths that we're sure are the right ones will turn out to be dead ends. We're going to need to change direction. But when we do it should be in a way that doesn't break your work.

We believe that the best tools are not created in a silo. They are created with the input and feedback of the people that use them. The community is a vital part of the process, from writing documentation, to testing, to contributing code and bug fixes. We are in this together.

docs.title: Why Themes Are Published Into Your App
docs.text: Most of Bonfire stays in vendor/ and changes when you run composer update. Themes are the exception. The installer gives your app its own copy, and from then on that copy is yours. This page explains why Bonfire works this way, what that gives you, and what it means when you update Bonfire.

docs.title: What happens at install
docs.text:
php spark bf:install copies Bonfire's Admin, App and Auth themes into a themes/ folder in your project root. It also publishes app/Config/Themes.php, whose $collections setting points at that folder.

From then on, your app renders only from themes/. The themes in vendor/lonnieezell/bonfire/themes/ are still there, but nothing reads them.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
A theme is the part of the admin you are most likely to want to change: the page layout, the header, the sidebar, the <x-…> view components, the CSS and the JavaScript. Because the files are in your app, you change them by editing them, the same way you'd edit any other view. There's no fork of the package to maintain and no override layer to learn.

Your edits are also safe. composer update replaces everything in vendor/, and it never touches themes/. This fits the rest of Bonfire's philosophy: give you a solid foundation, then get out of your way.

docs.title: What it costs
docs.text:
Your copy doesn't move when Bonfire does. It stays as it was when you published it, and it doesn't pick up the theme fixes and features in later releases.

Usually that's fine, but sometimes Bonfire's PHP code and its theme change together. A view may start using a new component, or a page may need a new CSS rule or a new section in master.php. An old copy of the theme doesn't have these, so the page breaks or looks wrong. In October 2026, for example, the Admin theme was redesigned, and Bonfire's admin views started using components that older copies didn't have.

So for Bonfire, a change to a theme file is a breaking change, even when your own PHP code works as before.

docs.title: How Bonfire tells you
docs.text:
Bonfire can't update your copy for you. It doesn't know which files you've changed, or how to merge your edits with its own. It tells you when a release needs you to look:

  • The changelog marks those releases with (breaking change) after the date, and names the files that changed.
  • After composer update, php spark notify:breaking-changes reads the changelog of the version you now have, and warns you once about any new breaking change since your last update.

The warning is a pointer to the changelog. Bonfire changes nothing on its own.

docs.title: What "re-publish" means
docs.text:
When the changelog says to re-publish a theme or copy a file, there is no command for it. You bring the new files from vendor/lonnieezell/bonfire/themes/ into themes/ and keep your own edits. If you never edited the theme, you can copy the whole folder over. If you did, you merge the two by hand.

How much work that is depends on how much of Bonfire's theme you've changed. If you keep your changes in a theme of your own, such as themes/MyAdmin for your own controllers, the Admin copy stays close to Bonfire's and is easy to replace.

When Bonfire updates shows how to compare your copy with Bonfire's.

docs.title: How Bonfire Fits Into a Request
docs.text: Bonfire doesn't replace CodeIgniter's request cycle. It hooks into it at a few points: it registers its modules with the autoloader, adds some filters, and gives your controllers a theme to render with. Everything else is a plain CodeIgniter request. This page walks through those points in the order a request meets them, so you know when your module's code runs and why.

docs.title: Before routing: module namespaces
docs.text:
On CodeIgniter's pre_system event, before the router runs, Bonfire registers every module folder with the autoloader: each folder in Bonfire's src/ (such as src/Users), and each folder inside the locations listed in Config\Bonfire::$appModules.

This is what makes a module feel like part of the app. CodeIgniter's auto-discovery looks in every registered folder, so it finds a module's Config/Routes.php, Config/Events.php and Config/Registrar.php without you listing them anywhere.

docs.title: The filter chain
docs.text:
Bonfire registers its filters through its Registrar, so an install picks them up without editing app/Config/Filters.php. They run in this order:

  1. online, on every request except /site-offline. When the site is offline, it sends visitors to /site-offline. Superadmins and users with the site.viewOffline permission browse the site as usual.
  2. session, on every URL under the admin area (ADMIN_AREA, admin by default). Shield's session filter sends guests to the login page.
  3. admin, on the same URLs. It sends logged-in users without the admin.access permission to the home page.
  4. bonfire, on every URL. It boots Bonfire, as described below.

The order matters. session and admin come before bonfire, so a visitor who may not enter the admin area is turned away before any module code runs.

After the controller has run, two more filters work on the response: alerts adds any queued alerts to the page, and consent adds the cookie consent banner to pages outside the admin area, when consent is turned on and the visitor hasn't given it yet.

docs.title: Booting: module discovery
docs.text:
The bonfire filter calls service('bonfire')->boot(), once per request. Booting first looks for modules in three places:

  • Core modules: the folders in Bonfire's own src/.
  • App modules: the folders inside each location in Config\Bonfire::$appModules.
  • Package modules: the directories listed in Config\Bonfire::$packageModules, one per Composer package.

Not every folder is a module. Bonfire only loads the ones that contain a Module.php, and makes one instance of each Module class. It caches the list of folders it found in the first two places, which is why a new module folder only appears after the cache expires or after php spark cache:clear.

docs.title: initAdmin() or initFront()
docs.text:
Next, Bonfire calls one method on every module. The URL decides which:

  • A path that is ADMIN_AREA or starts with ADMIN_AREA/ is an admin request, and every module gets initAdmin().
  • Any other request is a front-end request, and every module gets initFront().

Before an admin boot calls initAdmin(), Bonfire creates the admin's shared structures: the sidebar menu with its Content, Settings and Tools collections, the iconbar menu, and the dashboard's stats, charts and logs widgets. These exist only in admin requests, so initAdmin() is the place to add menu items and widgets. initFront() is for setup your module needs on public pages.

Because booting happens in a filter, it only happens where filters run. 404 pages, pages served from CodeIgniter's page cache, and CLI commands don't boot Bonfire on their own. Code that needs the admin set up outside a web request, such as a queue worker running an admin action, calls boot(true), which runs initAdmin() whatever the URL.

docs.title: Rendering: themes
docs.text:
By the time your controller runs, Bonfire has done its setup. The rest is ordinary CodeIgniter routing to your controller. Bonfire's part comes back when the controller renders a page.

A controller that extends AdminController renders with the Admin theme, and one that extends Bonfire's BaseController with the App theme. render() points the view renderer at the theme's folder, so the theme's layout and its <x-…> view components wrap your view. Those theme folders are your app's own copy, not Bonfire's. Why Themes Are Published Into Your App explains why.
